entries.title: Draft audit: C0048 uniform critical magnetization gap
entries.statement: DRAFT AUDIT CONCEPT; independent referee pending. For integer q>=3,d>=3, C0048 asks theta_w(p_c)>0 for the zero-field nearest-neighbor FK/Potts model on Z^d. With delta-spin coupling p=1-exp(-beta), normalized color-1 magnetization equals theta_w(p). Wired theta_w is the decreasing finite-box limit of continuous increasing connection probabilities, hence right continuous in p. A lower bound delta>0 must be uniform as p decreases to p_c. Such a bound proves critical ordering; positivity with a p-dependent bound tending to zero does not. The uniform gap, particularly q=d=3, remains unproved in this packet; current general openness is UNKNOWN.
assumptions: nearest-neighbor Z^d, unit ferromagnetic coupling, zero field
wired FK / monochromatic color-1 Potts boundary

entries.title: Draft audit: Positive FK edge conditionals do not imply percolation
entries.statement: DRAFT AUDIT CONCEPT; independent referee pending. For q>=1 and 0<p<1, a finite FK edge conditional, given any subset of the other edges, lies between a=p/(p+q(1-p)) and p. The bounds follow from the open/closed component-count ratio and the tower property. For integer d>=1, in wired boxes [-N,N]^d, integer N>=1, connection of the origin to the boundary is at most 2d*p*((2d-1)*p)^(N-1), by sequential path conditioning and a union bound. At q=3,d=3,p=1/10 all local edge conditionals are at least 1/28, yet the one-arm bound is (3/5)*2^(-(N-1)) and tends to zero. The example is subcritical and does not refute C0048. Local positivity alone cannot supply the uniform critical gap.
assumptions: only box boundary vertices are wired

entries.title: Draft audit: Fourth-cumulant mixing term and critical Legendre ratios
entries.statement: DRAFT AUDIT CONCEPT; independent referee pending. For a finite free zero-field Potts graph with N vertices and integer q>=3, let S=sum_v(1{sigma_v=1}-1/q), H_j=sum_FK_components |C|^j, c2=(q-1)/q^2 and c4=(q-1)(q^2-6q+6)/q^4. Independent uniform cluster colors conditional on FK give kappa4(S)=c4*E H4+3*c2^2*Var(H2). At q=3 the omitted mixture term is (4/27)*Var(H2). For P(h)=N^-1 log E exp(hS), chi=P''(0)>0 and local Legendre I, I'''(0)=-P'''(0)/chi^3 and I''''(0)=3*(P'''(0))^2/chi^5-P''''(0)/chi^4. P'''(0)>0 alone does not provide a uniform magnetization cubic. Passing to criticality requires controlled ratios and a remainder on a fixed magnetization interval. The corresponding actual-lattice potential input is unproved.
assumptions: independent uniform FK colors conditional on all edges

entries.title: Draft audit: An invariant cubic polynomial term with continuous onset
entries.statement: DRAFT AUDIT CONCEPT; independent referee pending. For real t and z in C, set r=|z| and F_t(z)=-t*r^2+r^(5/2)-Re(z^3)+r^4. Rotation by 2pi/3 and conjugation preserve F_t, giving the standard S3 action. The cubic polynomial term has a fixed nonzero coefficient. Put c=1-2/(3sqrt(3))>0; 1-s+s^3>=c for s>=0 gives F_t>=-t*r^2+c*r^(5/2). Thus zero is the unique global minimizer for t<=0. For t>0, small positive real z has negative value, and coercivity gives nonzero minimizers with radius at most (t/c)^2. All minimizers approach zero as t decreases to zero. This is a toy variational counterexample to the bare invariant-cubic criterion, not a lattice Potts model. The fractional term prevents a uniform quartic Taylor remainder.
assumptions: no identification with the lattice constrained free energy
